rationale: Psalm 105:14-15 (BSB) says that God 'rebuked kings on their behalf: “Do not touch My anointed ones! Do no harm to My prophets!”', and 1 Chronicles 16:21-22 repeats the same lines. The psalm names Abraham, Isaac and Jacob just before (105:9-10) and calls them 'strangers in the land' (105:12), but it names no king, no wife and no episode. Two Hebrew words tie it to Genesis 20 on Bible Hub's interlinear: naga, 'touch' (Strong's 5060), which God uses in 20:6 ('I did not let you touch her') and Abimelech in 26:11 (BSB 'Whoever harms'), and nabi, 'prophet' (Strong's 5030), whose first occurrence in Bible Hub's concordance is 20:7, the only verse in Genesis where Abraham, or anyone, is called a prophet. Commentators on both passages make the link: the Cambridge Bible on Genesis 20:7 calls Psalm 105:14-15 'A comment on this passage', Keil and Delitzsch on Genesis 20 cite Psalm 105:15, Ellicott on the psalm says the poet 'found it expressly conferred on Abraham in Genesis 20:7', and Keil and Delitzsch on Psalm 105:14 say the poet 'has the three histories of the preservation of the wives of the patriarchs in his mind'; the Cambridge Bible on Psalm 105:15 says of 'Touch not' that 'The phrase is suggested by Genesis 20:6'; Jamieson-Fausset-Brown instead tie 'Touch not' to Genesis 26:11, and the Pulpit Commentary notes that 'The actual words of this verse do not occur in Genesis'. Graded allusion rather than explicit_reference, following conn-gen10-divided-deut32, because the psalm evokes the episodes through shared vocabulary without naming them, and strong because the shared Hebrew is checkable and Barnes, Poole, Gill, Jamieson-Fausset-Brown and the Pulpit Commentary on Psalm 105:14 name or cite Pharaoh and Abimelech (or Genesis 12:17 and 20:3) for the rebuked kings.
